q: In FortiManager 7.6, what is the difference between a Normal mode ADOM and a Backup mode ADOM? Under which specific conditions does a FortiGate unit in a Backup mode ADOM send a configuration revision to the FortiManager?
kp: Normal mode ADOMs are read/write: you can push configuration changes from FortiManager to managed devices
Backup mode ADOMs store device configurations; FortiManager cannot push new configuration changes directly (changes are made via scripts on the device, or the device GUI/CLI)
Revision is sent when: configuration change and session timeout
Revision is sent when: configuration change and log out
Revision is sent when: configuration change and reboot
Revision is sent when: manual configuration backup from the managed device

q: In a Backup mode ADOM, what setting must be enabled on the FortiManager to allow configuration backups from the FortiGate device CLI, and what is the exact CLI command?
kp: fcp-cfg-service must be enabled
config system global
set fcp-cfg-service enable

q: In FortiManager, which modules share the object database to provide policy configuration information to FortiGates, and which modules use their own protocols to communicate directly with managed devices? Name at least three of the first and two of the second.
kp: Object database shared by Policies & Objects (any three from: Policies & Objects, AP Manager, VPN Manager, Extender Manager, FortiSwitch Manager)
Modules using direct protocols (any two from: FortiGuard, FortiAnalyzer features, Device Manager)

q: What is the maximum size of a FortiManager high availability (HA) cluster, and what are the key requirements for forming one?
kp: Maximum of five units: one primary unit with up to four backup/secondary units
All units in the cluster must be of the same FortiManager series
FortiAnalyzer Features must be disabled on the FortiManager before forming an HA cluster
Geographic redundancy is supported: primary and secondary units can be in different locations

q: According to the FortiManager 7.6 Ports document, which TCP ports are used for FGFM management between FortiGate and FortiManager (IPv4 and IPv6), and which port is used for OFTP logging of all Fortinet products?
kp: FGFM management IPv4: TCP/541
FGFM management IPv6: TCP/542 (starting in FortiManager 7.4.1)
OFTP logging: TCP/514

q: What command can you use on a FortiManager unit to view the supported maximum values for that model, and what does the FortiManager 7.6.8 Maximum Values document say about the maximum values table it provides?
kp: print tablesize command
The document's table reflects maximum values for a FortiManager virtual machine as an example; supported values depend on the actual model

q: What does the policy consistency check (policy check tool) in FortiManager verify across the policy packages of an ADOM? Name the four object conditions it checks.
kp: Object duplication: two objects with identical definitions
Object shadowing: a higher priority object completely encompasses another object of the same type
Object overlap: one object partially overlaps another object of the same type (partially shadowed)
Object orphaning: an object defined but not used anywhere

q: In a Normal mode ADOM, how do FortiGate units keep their configuration synchronized with FortiManager? State the query interval and what is sent when a change is detected.
kp: FortiGate units query their own configuration every 5 seconds
When a configuration change is detected, the FortiGate sends a diff revision of the change to the FortiManager using the FGFM protocol

q: What does the FortiManager & FortiAnalyzer 7.6.8 Log Reference document provide, and what log information categories does it cover?
kp: Detailed information about FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer log messages, which provide an audit log of user actions
Log types and subtypes for both FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer
Log message examples (e.g., event log message examples with message breakdown)
Priority levels

q: Besides centralized configuration management, name two other roles a FortiManager installation can play in an organization's infrastructure, and how many devices/VDOMs can a single FortiManager interface scale to manage?
kp: On-site FortiGuard Distribution Server (FDS) so managed devices and FortiClient agents can download signature/update files locally
Optional FortiAnalyzer features for analyzing logs of managed devices and generating reports
Scales to manage 10,000 or more devices and virtual domains (VDOMs) from a single FortiManager interface
